title: Scheduler routing misassignment causing long-tail token latency — follow-up & mitigation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed a sustained increase in 95/99th token latency for a subset of hosted API traffic after the scheduler change deployed in runtime-2.4.0. Impact affected ~7% of requests routed to dedicated pools using mixed-kernel profiles. Latency spikes correlated with kernel misassignment where small-sequence requests were routed to a slow fused-attention kernel for certain model variants, causing long-tail queuing and KV-cache inefficiencies.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC: First anomaly alerted via latency SLO dashboard (console-runtime/latency).
- 2026-03-09 03:25 UTC: On-call rotated, initial triage pointed to increased queue lengths on a subset of worker groups.
- 2026-03-09 04:10 UTC: Rollback of scheduler heuristics (hotfix) applied for affected pools; 95th latency reduced to baseline within 12 minutes.
- 2026-03-09 06:00 UTC: Post-rollback monitoring and data collection.

Root cause (summary):
A recent heuristic change to kernel affinity scoring prioritized throughput for mixed-length workloads by biasing towards fused-attention kernels when predicted sequence-length distribution included long tails. An off-by-one bug in the affinity comparator caused requests with predicted short sequences to be classified as "mixed-long" under certain histogram edge-cases, routing them to a fused-attention path that has worse latency for short sequences on the deployed GPU microcode. The scheduler did not validate kernel compatibility with an explicit sequence-length cutoff for that model family.

Mitigations performed: 
- Immediate rollback of the affinity bias flags for affected pools (runtime-2.4.0 -> runtime-2.4.0-rollback-1).
- Canary patch to add an explicit sequence-length validation check in scheduler routing logic.
- Temporary pinning of model variants to CPU/kernel profiles that preserve low-latency path for short sequences.

Decisions & trade-offs: 
- Chose rollback + conservative validation instead of progressive gradual rollout because customer impact reached P0 thresholds. This increases short-term predictability at the cost of temporarily lower throughput for a narrow set of workloads.
- Deferred kernel microcode tuning (requires vendor coordination) until after local fixes to avoid blocking customer-facing mitigation.

Open questions: 
- Do we need an automated test harness that simulates mixed-length sequence distributions for the scheduler?
- Should affinity scoring be decoupled from kernel selection and exposed as a tunable policy per-customer?

Linked artifacts and telemetry: see links field for dashboards, PRs, and incident notes.
